record.paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
record.original_question: Can one define a subclass of holomorphic mappings f: C^m -> P^n that gives a reasonable geometric and analytic value-distribution theory in higher codimension: every map in the subclass should satisfy the Nevanlinna inequality N(D,r) <= T(r)+O(1), the Liouville-type relation integral over D in |D| of delta(D) dmu(D)=0 for divisors in a complete linear system, and the functorial restriction property that f restricted to C^k remains in the subclass whenever f:C^m -> P^n is in the subclass?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}^m \to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a holomorphic mapping. For an effective divisor $D$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ whose support does not contain the image of $f$, let $N(D,r)$ denote the counting function of $f^{-1}(D)$ and $T(r)$ the (Cartan) characteristic function of $f$, defined in the usual sense of Nevanlinna value-distribution theory. For a complete linear system $|D|$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ with measure $d\mu$ induced by a unitary structure, let $\delta(D)=1-\limsup_{r\to\infty} N(D,r)/T(r)$ be the Nevanlinna defect.

Construct, for every pair $(m,n)$ with $1\le m\le n$, a non-empty class $\mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ of holomorphic maps $f:\mathbb{C}^m \to \mathbb{P}^n$ such that all of the following hold:

(i) (First Main Theorem inequality) For every $f \in \mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ and every effective divisor $D$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ whose support omits $f(\mathbb{C}^m)$,
$$N(D,r) \le T(r) + O(1).$$

(ii) (Liouville-type defect relation) For every $f \in \mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ and every complete linear system $|D|$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$,
$$\int_{D \in |D|} \delta(D)\, d\mu(D) = 0.$$

(iii) (Functorial restriction) For every $f \in \mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ and every linear embedding $\iota:\mathbb{C}^k \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}^m$ with $1\le k\le m$, the restriction $f \circ \iota$ belongs to $\mathcal{F}_{k,n}$.

Determine whether such a class $\mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ exists in higher codimension (i.e., when $m<n$), and if so, give an explicit characterization that is broad enough to be geometrically and analytically natural.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying a natural subclass of holomorphic mappings from $\mathbb{C}^m$ to $\mathbb{P}^n$ in higher codimension that simultaneously satisfies a First Main Theorem inequality, a Liouville-type integrated defect relation, and a functorial restriction property is a long-standing program in higher-dimensional Nevanlinna theory. Existing approaches (Griffiths, Ahlfors, Stoll, and the differentiably non-degenerate framework) handle special cases (equidimensional or non-degenerate maps), and the Ahlfors theorem is noted as one of the few global treatments of higher codimension. No general construction satisfying all three properties simultaneously appears in the literature; the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Nevanlinna Theory and Holomorphic Mappings Between Algebraic Varieties (Griffiths)
status_evidence.snippet: Extension of Nevanlinna theory to holomorphic mappings between higher-dimensional varieties; treatment focuses largely on the equidimensional / non-degenerate case.
status_evidence.claim: The higher-codimension Nevanlinna theory is only partially developed; standard formulations require non-degeneracy.

status_evidence.title: Ahlfors' contribution to the theory of meromorphic functions (Eremenko)
status_evidence.snippet: The Ahlfors theorem is one of the few instances where higher codimension has been dealt with globally in complex-analytic geometry.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-codimension global value distribution remains largely undeveloped, supporting that the proposed program is still open.
